tool.name: Holomics
tool.description: Interactive single- and multi-omics analysis with mixOmics
tool.command: mkdir -p holomics_inputs && cp '$manifest' holomics_inputs/manifest.json && export HOLOMICS_STARTUP_LOG='$startup_log' && exec /usr/local/bin/holomics-entrypoint

configfiles.configfile: #import json #set $entries = [] #for $block in $blocks #set $entry = {"name": str($block.block_name), "filename": str($block.matrix.name), "path": str($block.matrix), "separator": str($block.separator), "transpose": str($block.transpose) == "true", "prepared": str($block.prepared) == "true"} #silent $entries.append($entry) #end for #set $label_entry = None #if $labels #set $label_entry = {"path": str($labels), "separator": str($label_separator)} #end if $json.dumps({"blocks": $entries, "labels": $label_entry})

param.name: matrix
param.label: Numeric feature table
param.help: First column: sample IDs. Header: feature IDs. Normalize measurements appropriately before import.

param.name: transpose
param.label: Features in rows, samples in columns

param.name: prepared
param.label: Already prepared for direct multi-omics analysis
param.help: Also makes this block available to pairwise sPLS and DIABLO. No normalization or filtering is applied during Galaxy import. Otherwise use the original single-omics reduction first.

param.name: labels
param.label: Sample labels
param.help: Exactly two columns: sample ID and categorical class. IDs must match all omics tables.

tool.help:
**Holomics**, developed by the original Holomics authors, provides PCA, PLS-DA, sparse feature selection, pairwise sPLS and DIABLO integration in a Shiny app. The original interface and analysis workflows are unchanged.
Select named omics tables and matching sample labels from your Galaxy history on the launch form. They load automatically into the original application. Tables must have identical sample sets; rows are aligned by sample ID without silently dropping samples. All launch inputs are optional, so the original **Upload data** tab remains available. Supply numeric feature tables, not raw reads. Mark prepared blocks to use them directly for sPLS and DIABLO; otherwise first reduce them through the original single-omics workflow.
**Exports:** each result has separate **Download** and **Send to Galaxy** buttons. Download saves only to your browser. Send to Galaxy uploads only to the current history. Results are also staged in a collection collected when the session stops; this is the fallback if the live upload fails. Wait for uploads before stopping the interactive tool. No project checkpoints or extra analysis modules are added.
Statistical methods and validation are those of the original application. Exploratory separation plots are not independent predictive validation.
### Step-by-step two-omics example
1. Upload two numeric tables and a labels table to Galaxy. Example names: `Transcriptomics.csv`, `Proteomics.csv`, `Labels.csv`. The omics tables have samples in rows, features in columns, headers, and sample IDs in column one. Labels have exactly two columns: sample ID and class. All files must describe the same sample set. Normalize measurements appropriately before analysis. 2. Add two **Omics block** entries on this launch form. Name them **Transcriptomics** and **Proteomics**, and select their respective tables. For CSV examples select **Comma**. Leave transpose unchecked when samples are rows. For already prepared example data, check **Already prepared for direct multi-omics analysis** on both blocks. 3. Select `Labels.csv` under **Sample labels** and **Comma** as its separator. Run the tool, then open Holomics from Galaxy's Active Interactive Tools page. 4. In **Upload data**, confirm both blocks are listed; switch to **Labels/Classes** to confirm **Galaxy labels**. Inputs are loaded automatically: do not upload Galaxy's internal `.dat` files again. 5. Optionally explore each block under **Single-omics → PCA**, selecting **Galaxy labels**. For unprepared data, use the original feature-selection workflow first, then select the resulting reduced blocks for integration. 6. Open **Multi-omics**. Select both blocks and **Galaxy labels**. Start with two components (where supported) and the app's suggested design matrix value. 7. Inspect pairwise correlations, sample plots, loadings and heatmaps. Click **Tune parameters**, wait for **DIABLO tuned**, then compare its settings, error rates and plots with the initial model. Do not change inputs while tuning. 8. Click **Download** to save a result locally, or **Send to Galaxy** to export it to your history. Wait for the Galaxy dataset to reach `ok` before stopping the interactive session. The collected results collection is a fallback.
Use **Pairwise** for two-block sPLS instead of class-guided DIABLO. Do not treat an original block and its reduced copy as two independent omics layers. Demo separation is exploratory, not an independently validated prediction result.
